name: Etruscan wheel-thrown pottery
description: Potters in Etruria began throwing vessels on a wheel alongside changes in clay refinement and firing.

impact.note: Etruria adopted wheel throwing, making an existing craft faster and more uniform across one region, with later Italian wares as its successors.

date.label: Seventh century BCE, approximate
date.basis: The source reports the date for this scoped event or archaeological context.

events.statement: The museum account places wheel throwing alongside seventh-century developments in Etruscan pottery.

evidence.supports: The museum account places wheel throwing alongside seventh-century developments in Etruscan pottery.
The source attributes this contribution to Etruscan potters.

events.caveats: The source does not specify wheel speed; the date is an approximate contextual association, not a dated first use.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated case currently researched, not a claim of the capability’s original invention or global priority.

caveats: The account is a broad art-historical summary, not a dated production record for one throwing workshop or proof of the first wheel anywhere.

research.note: Independent review checked the cited Met publication, p. 86, through an accessible text transcription. The account associates wheel throwing with seventh-century pottery developments but does not specify wheel speed or establish the precise date of its introduction.
